processing: Little is recorded for this name; a fully oxidised black tea, and the 'golden needle' name points to a bud-rich pick, as with other needle-style blacks.
harvest_season: Not specifically recorded; bud-rich black teas are typically spring pickings.
appearance_dry: As the name suggests, slender needles with golden down.
appearance_liquor: Typically a clear orange-red for a bud-grade Fujian black tea.
appearance_wet: Typically soft buds in a bright reddish copper.
taste_profile: No detailed tasting record exists for this name; bud-heavy Fujian blacks are typically honeyed and smooth, with little bitterness.

brewing.notes: General advice for bud-heavy black tea: cooler water and short steeps.

vintage_note: Nothing specific is recorded for this name. Black teas of this kind are usually sold as a recent spring harvest, with the budded grades priced highest; ask for the year, and drink within a couple of years.
description:
Bai Lin Jin Zhen, golden needle from Bailin, is a black tea name attached to the Bailin area of Fuding in northeast Fujian. It turns up in specialist tea catalogues, but very little has been written about it as a distinct tea.

Its obvious relative by name is Bailin Gongfu. Jin zhen simply means golden needle, a name usually given to a bud-heavy grade, so it is fair to read this as a bud-led Bailin tea, though that link is an inference from the name.

In the cup, expect what is typical of bud-grade Fujian blacks rather than a documented house style: a sweet, soft tea with honey and gentle malt. Keep the water slightly below the boil and the steeps short; a downy tea goes flat when it is pushed hard.

Because the name has no firm standard, ask the seller where it was picked and in what season. If you want a better documented reference point, try Bailin Gongfu alongside it.
history: Little is documented about this tea by name, and no date or maker can be tied to it. The local black tea tradition around Bailin is better recorded: Bailin Gongfu is said to date from the 1850s, when tea merchants in Fuding gathered black tea from the surrounding districts for finishing at Bailin, and a 2024 group standard now covers it.
